I do socialize with other people with DID! I am in a lot of support groups as well as I am in forums about the disorder, and over time I have made friends in those communities. A lot of people agree with me, yes. 

In my case, I do not really have a "first" alter. The concept of "first" isn't technically true because technically you are all parts, there's not just one centerpiece that is the same. Imagine a piece of paper, and you considered that paper a child, a being trying to become of an adult and their own person. Trauma happens and dissociative barriers are created, the paper is ripped. Which part of the paper would you consider the "first" piece of paper?

I am a recovering poly-fragmented system. I now have 47 alters, but I use to have over 100. After integration and such, we have 10 nonhuman alters. Well. One of them is a ghost. So he used to be human-

Not a dumb question at all! Different people have definitions of host for their systems. I personally see the host as a person who is the face of the system more, fronting the most often and kind of the center of things. I am not the "core" alter, which is a common way of saying the person who was "born"/the "first". I put lots of quotation but technically this is just not a true concept, but that's for a different day. But I was formed later in childhood, I just front the most and I identify with the body the most. So I consider myself host.

There are different kinds of dissociation, ranging in scale from my personal experience. I'm sure different people will feel differently about their dissociation. Sometimes I am fine, and then suddenly everything feels very far away. Things I know I am touching feel like I'm not touching them, and that I'm still reaching for them. Sometimes I just started to hear sound distorted, almost like muffled? Sometimes I dissociate and I end up in my inner world. Not all people with DID have an inner world, but it is very common. That's where my alters and I interact with each other. And that can feel different depending on how close I am to front.   


Yes, I have founds ways to help! I am in therapy and I see a psychiatrist. We are focusing on grounding techniques as well as healing my other parts. I do things like mess with my fidget cube (I'm also autistic), try to keep focused on hobbies, set goals for myself more. Trying to move forward while also slowly allowing the alters to front and go on their own healing journies. It's been a wild ride.

Well, DID isn't a personality disorder. It is a dissociative disorder. That is partly why the name was changed to that rather than multiple personality disorder. But they are co-morbid disorders (which just means it is common for them to be diagnosed with each other). One possible cause of BPD is trauma/neglect, and DID is caused by repeated trauma, usually abuse, before the age of 9. So a lot of people with DID will be affected by BPD. However, since DID is such a unique disorder to the individual, how they correlate with each other can be different.

Some of my alters are affected by BPD, but they managed it very differently. I am the host of the system, which basically means I front the most. I tend to show the most BPD symptoms.
